data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies 'reduced humidity over impervious urban surfaces' as a core driver of the cross-city UHI gap, asserting the gap 'scales with aridity.' This causal claim contradicts the most widely documented cross-city pattern: nocturnal UHIs are most pronounced in humid, well-watered cities, not arid ones. The standard UHI-climate literature (e.g., the classic humid vs. arid oasis comparison) shows that in arid cities the rural surroundings also lack evapotranspiration and vegetation, so the urban–rural latent-heat differential shrinks or even reverses; it is in humid cities that paving over vegetated, well-watered land removes a large rural latent sink, yielding a large differential. By making the gap scale positively with aridity, the target likely gets the sign wrong for the cross-city modulator the problem asks for.
